excerpt: Torq sells an AI security operations (SOC) and hyperautomation platform. Its 2026 Series D, what the product does and alternatives.
content:
Torq makes software for security operations centres (SOCs). Security teams receive a constant flood of alerts from their tools; Torq's platform uses AI agents and automated workflows to triage those alerts, investigate them and take response actions, so analysts only handle the cases that need a person. Its homepage line sums up the pitch: every alert needs attention, but not every alert needs a human. It calls the approach agentic SecOps combined with hyperautomation.

The product has two main parts: a no-code and low-code workflow builder that connects to a company's existing security and IT tools, and an AI SOC layer with agents, one of which Torq calls Socrates, that work through cases and report back. Customers named by SiliconANGLE include Marriott International, PepsiCo, Procter & Gamble, Siemens, Uber and Virgin Atlantic.

Torq was founded in 2020. Its cofounder and chief executive is Ofer Smadari. On 11 January 2026 it announced a $140 million Series D at a $1.2 billion valuation, led by Merlin Ventures with existing investors Evolution Equity Partners, Notable Capital, Bessemer Venture Partners, Insight Partners and Greenfield Partners. SiliconANGLE reported that this brought its total funding to $332 million and that the money would go into wider adoption of the AI platform and its go-to-market work, including selling to the US federal government.

Torq does not publish prices. It sells to mid-size and large enterprises through demos and contracts. Small teams without a dedicated security operations function are unlikely to need it. Buyers comparing it with rivals usually look at how many of their existing tools it connects to and how much of the triage it can take over safely.

This profile is put together from the company's own pages and published reporting, checked on 15 October 2026. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.
